deep.reconstruction:
Notation (E477): ∫(1/z^m)(1/y^n) = Σ_{z≥1} z^{-m} Σ_{y≤z} y^{-n} =: ζ*(m,n), the non-strict double zeta value, equal to ζ(m,n)+ζ(m+n) with ζ(m,n)=Σ_{z>y} z^{-m}y^{-n}. ∫1/z^m = ζ(m). The page continues 'Ordo septimus' (weight m+n=8) of Euler's second method. That method writes ζ(m)ζ(n)−ζ(m+n) as a binomially weighted combination of products ζ(a)ζ(b) and sums ζ*(a,b), which are shuffle-type relations. Euler then reduces the result with the first-method (stuffle) relation ζ*(a,b)+ζ*(b,a)=ζ(a)ζ(b)+ζ(a+b), with ζ*(4,4)=½ζ(4)²+½ζ(8).

Case m=7, n=1. The last line Σ_{k=1}^{7} ζ*(k,8−k) becomes ζ1ζ7+ζ2ζ6+ζ3ζ5+½ζ4²+(7/2)ζ8. This is correct; the divergent ζ(1)ζ(7) cancels formally against the left side. Combined with the previous page's −2ζ2ζ6−2ζ4²−2ζ6ζ2 it gives ζ*(7,1)=3ζ2ζ6−ζ3ζ5+(3/2)ζ4²−(9/2)ζ8, which equals (9/4)ζ8−ζ3ζ5≈1.01273. The page prints 2ζ2ζ6−ζ3ζ5+½ζ4²−(9/2)ζ8.

Case m=6, n=2. The expansion gives ζ*(2,6)+2ζ*(3,5)+3ζ*(4,4)+4ζ*(5,3)+6ζ*(6,2)+12ζ*(7,1)=13ζ6ζ2+ζ8+6ζ4². This reduces to 2ζ*(5,3)+5ζ*(6,2)+12ζ*(7,1)=12ζ6ζ2−2ζ3ζ5+(9/2)ζ4²−(7/2)ζ8. I checked it numerically: both sides ≈19.34579.

Case m=5, n=3. The expansion gives ζ*(3,5)+3ζ*(4,4)+7ζ*(5,3)+15ζ*(6,2)+30ζ*(7,1)=30ζ6ζ2+ζ5ζ3+6ζ4²−ζ8. It reduces (next page) to 6ζ*(5,3)+15ζ*(6,2)+30ζ*(7,1)=30ζ6ζ2+(9/2)ζ4²−(7/2)ζ8. Numerically both sides ≈51.961.

Purpose: find all weight-8 double sums in closed form. On the next page Euler finds that only ζ*(7,1) and one combination 2ζ*(5,3)+5ζ*(6,2) are determined, plus the checks 6ζ4²=7ζ8 and 2ζ2ζ6+ζ4²=(9/2)ζ8. This is consistent with the modern fact that ζ(5,3) is the first double zeta value not known to reduce to products of single zetas.
errors: Case m=7,n=1: the printed result ∫1/z^7(1/y)=2∫1/z^2·∫1/z^6−∫1/z^3·∫1/z^5+½∫1/z^4·∫1/z^4−(9/2)∫1/z^8 is wrong. It evaluates to −(7/12)ζ8−ζ3ζ5<0. The previous page's own equation gives 3∫1/z^2·∫1/z^6−∫1/z^3·∫1/z^5+(3/2)∫1/z^4·∫1/z^4−(9/2)∫1/z^8=(9/4)ζ8−ζ3ζ5. Euler's later comparison on p.160 ('2∫1/z^2·∫1/z^6+∫1/z^4·∫1/z^4=(9/2)∫1/z^8') follows only from the corrected coefficients (3 and 3/2). So this is a misprint or copying slip, not an error in reasoning.
Formal use of the divergent ∫1/z (harmonic series) in the 'ultima linea'. It cancels against ζ(7)ζ(1) on the left, so the result is unaffected, but the step is not rigorous.

ideas.what: Non-strict double sums ζ*(m,n) and their evaluation at weight 8
ideas.modern_name: double zeta values / multiple harmonic (Euler) sums

ideas.what: Combining two independent families of linear relations (first method: stuffle-type ζ*(a,b)+ζ*(b,a)=ζ(a)ζ(b)+ζ(a+b); second method: partial-fraction, shuffle-type expansions with binomial weights)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler for both families; systematized by Zagier, Ihara–Kaneko–Zagier (2006)

ideas.what: Weight 8 yields only one relation between ζ(5,3) and ζ(6,2), not separate values
ideas.modern_name: irreducibility of ζ(5,3); dimension of weight-8 MZV space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler's observation; modern theory by Zagier, Broadhurst–Kreimer, Borwein–Bradley–Broadhurst

deep.surprise_reason: This is standard, well-studied E477 material on double zeta values at weight 8. The only finding is a coefficient misprint in the m=7,n=1 result, and Euler's own later comparison implicitly corrects it.
